newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill buyers hanging on for next rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill buyers hanging on for next rate rise.

text.p: Manila's secondary market for Treasury bills were lacklustre on Friday, with plenty of sellers but most buyers prefering to wait for rates to go up gain next week, traders said.
"Trading is just limited to servicing clients' requirements," a dealer said.
Traders said banks would rather sell ahead of the T-bill auction on Monday.
"The expectation next Monday is that rates could be up by 150 basis points on all tenors based on the secondary market trading today," the same dealer said.
"The market realizes the overnight rate will not go down that fast," he added.
The Central Bank on Wednesday raised its key overnight rate by nine points to 24 percent to stave off speculation on the peso caused by Thailand's de facto devaluation.
A Reuters poll of five financial institutions gave offers of 11/12.25 percent for three-month bills, 11.50/12.50 percent for six months, and 11.90/13.50 percent for one year.
The average interbank call loan rate moved up to 24.40625 percent from 24.3125 percent, touching a high of 26.5 percent from a previous 26 percent.
